newsitem.title: GERMANY: German IBIS DAX index ends trade at higher levels.
newsitem.headline: German IBIS DAX index ends trade at higher levels.

text.p: German shares continued a surprise rally on Monday to end afternoon electronic trade higher, despite early fears of a collapse amid doubts about the future of EMU and a left-wing French victory in Sunday's poll.
At the end of the day the IBIS DAX index, which tracks electronic trade in 30 blue-chip shares, ended at 3,596.40 points, up 33.67 points or 0.95 percent, off highs of earlier in the session.
Meanwhile the June DAX future contract ended up 44 points at 3,607.
"Germany should have been down a lot today, because of the French election and doubts about the euro, but instead it's rallying. A lot is coming from the dollar," a German share trader said.

Propping up the market was the strong dollar, which was trading at or near 1.73 marks in late afternoon trade. The IBIS DAX passed the psychologically important 3,600-point barrier earlier and generally stayed near that level over the day.
The market was also able to withstand most downward pressure from Wall Street, where the Dow Jones Industrial index was weaker in early trade.

"Some of the rise in the market could be coming from the futures side, because there is not a lot of underlying cash business around. Last week it was the derivatives side which drove everything," the trader said.
Among the gainers in afternoon IBIS trade were those stocks influenced by the strong dollar, especially the chemicals sector.
There were big volumes seen in German chemicals groups BASF AG, which rose 1.50 marks to 64.40, Bayer AG, up 90 pfennigs to 67.80 marks and Hoechst AG, up 1.20 marks at 67.70 marks.
Banking stocks were also favoured, with Deutsche Bank AG up 66 pfennigs at 96.52 marks and Commerzbank AG up 30 pfennigs at 48.35 marks.
Drug group Schering AG performed well, ending up 3.60 marks at 175.60 marks, as did carmaker Volkswagen AG, up 20.70 marks at 1,125.70 marks.
